newsitem.title: THAILAND: GOLF-THAIS SPLASH OUT AND CELEBRATE WOODS'S WIN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-THAIS SPLASH OUT AND CELEBRATE WOODS'S WIN.

text.p: Thailand cheered Tiger Woods's victory in the U.S. Masters golf tournament on Monday, but his record-breaking feat had to share centre stage with merrymakers splashing their way into the new year.
Woods, whose mother Kultida was born in Thailand, caused a sensation when he visited the country to play in February.
"I think a lot of people stayed up during the night to watch (the Masters) on TV," said Pathai Bunrungrad, manager of the Golfer Driving Range. "I think this will further help golf in Thailand."
Television and radio stations on Monday led their news bulletins with reports of 21-year-old Woods's 18-under-par Masters tournament triumph on Sunday in Augusta, Georgia.
Woods is the youngest player ever to win the competition and he did it with a record 12-stroke margin.
But the victory appeared overshadowed by celebrations for the traditional four-day Songkran holiday, in which people splash their way into the Thai new year with good-natured water fights.

In Thailand, soccer and boxing are the most popular spectator sports. Golf is growing in popularity but primarily remains a game for tourists and the wealthy with a typical $50 round beyond the means of the vast majority of the 60 million population.
The record-breaking style of Woods's win and his sporting prowess were more significant than his Thai connections, many golf observers told Reuters.
"It's the win, and the way it was won, which is most important. The most important thing for many people is that he is simply a fantastic golfer," said a local sports editor.
Golf industry executives said they hoped the win might boost interest in Thai golf and perhaps even preface a major Thai victory within a few years.
"It's clearly good news for golf in Thailand," Kitti Komthongsathid, managing director of the Golf Course Membership Exchange, said of Woods's win.
"I think some time soon, maybe within the next 10 years, it might be possible to see a Thai golfer, rather than an American-Thai golfer, do the same."
